plan_a_advantages: More frequent easy runs could be beneficial for recovery and maintaining a consistent training volume.
The shorter run distances might be suitable for an athlete who is new to trail running or has limited time.
plan_b_advantages: Includes tempo runs, a crucial element for developing speed and lactate threshold, which is essential for faster trail running.
The longer runs at an easy pace build endurance and trail-specific fitness more effectively than the shorter runs in Plan A.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates tempo runs and longer, sustained efforts, directly addressing the need for increased speed and trail endurance – key components of trail running performance. Plan A, while consistent, primarily focuses on easy runs, which, while beneficial for building a base, won't significantly challenge the athlete to improve their speed or ability to handle longer distances at a faster pace. Plan B’s structured approach with threshold work and longer runs will provide a more targeted stimulus for improvement.
